steps.description: Implement the family function for two constraint families (rigid linear PDE and fat random polynomial), perform capacity scans with width h=2..64 across multiple seeds, verify the rigid anchor at low width, and report N_c(w) trends to classify each family as rigid (finite small N_c with flat/decreasing trend) or fat (unreachable).

plans.objective: [DIM: structural] The "rigid" constraint family corresponds to a subspace of affine functions ($f(x) = ax+b$) which has a solution dimension of 2, therefore a small network width ($h \ge 2$) should achieve zero violation on held-out points as $w$ increases, exhibiting a flat $N_c(w)$ trend.

steps.description: The previous iteration (iter 5) reported a surprise of 1.0, indicating a significant discrepancy between the predicted rigid family behavior (zero violation at small width) and actual results. This suggests the hypothesis about the affine function subspace may not hold under the experimental constraints, or there are implementation issues in the family construction. I will explore the problem by systematically investigating: (1) whether the rigid family is properly constructed with affine functions f(x)=ax+b, (2) whether the data normalization is correct (y/yv must be O(1) for 1e-3 threshold to be meaningful), (3) whether the held-out points are properly separated from training points, and (4) whether the network training is converging properly. This exploration will help identify the root cause of the failure before proceeding to full-scale experiments.
